main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Bindu Madhav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Supreme, Central Protector Form at Panchganga Ghat
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> BINDU MADHAV
As per directions of Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu travelled from Mandarachal to Kashi with a divine mission of making King Divodas leave Kashi (Kindly read Divodaseshwar).

After having accomplished his mission, Lord Vishnu was enjoying the serene beauty of Kashi, Pancha Nada Teerth, Padodak Teerth and other places. At Pancha Nada Teerth, he came across one extremely lean looking Sage who was undergoing Tapas.

Lord Vishnu in his divine form approached the Sage whose name was Agni Bindu and stood in front of him. The Sage, on seeing the Lord in person, was ecstatic and he prostrated before the Lord. The Sage then started singing praises of the Lord.

The Sage addressed the Lord by various names like Mukunda, Madusudan, Madhav, Narayan, Rama Bhadran, Chatur Bhuj, Janardhan etc. The Sage also mentioned that those who worship Lord Vishnu with Tulsi leaves or garland made of Tulsi Leaves will get lots of blessings.

After having sung all praises about Lord Vishnu, Agni Bindu Rishi stood silently with folded hands. Lord Vishnu asked the Sage to seek any divine boon. The Sage, in reply, sought only one thing: that Lord Vishnu should always be available in the vicinity of Pancha Nada Teerth.

Lord Vishnu granted accordingly. He further stated that Kashi is a Punya Kshetra and devotees can achieve several kinds of Siddhi by staying in Kashi. Lord Vishnu further told that he would stay in Kashi as long as Kashi is present and there will be no destruction of Kashi, as this holy city is situated atop the Trishul (Trident) of Lord Shiva. Therefore, even Maha Pralay (great deluge) cannot destroy the city.

Agni Bindu Rishi was extremely happy at this and sought one more divine boon from Lord Vishnu. He desired that Lord Vishnu should always be available in the vicinity of Pancha Nada Teerth in the name of the Sage. Further, a devotee who takes bath in Pancha Nada Teerth and even if he dies elsewhere, he should attain Moksha. The Sage also sought that a devotee who bathes in Pacha Nada Teerth and worships Lord Vishnu should be blessed with wealth and prosperity.

Lord Vishnu agreed to the request of the Sage. He stated that henceforth he (Lord) will be known as Bindu Madhav in Pancha Nada Teerth. By his presence, the Teerth will be extremely Sacred and devotees who bathe in this Teerth and honour learned persons, will be blessed with wealth and prosperity.

The Teerth, which is capable of cleansing all Sins, will be called as Bindu Teerth. A person may have committed various sins, knowingly or unknowingly. But if, during the Kartik Month, he religiously bathes in Pancha Nada Teerth and worships Bindu Madhav, he will attain Mukti.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 60 has given in detail the importance of Kartik Month in respect to Pancha Nada Teerth. Lord Visweshwar himself regularly takes bath in this Teerth during Kartik Month.
(BINDU MADHAV)

Lord Vishnu further stated that he (Lord) was called as Aadi Madhav in Sat Yug, he should be worshipped as Ananda Madhav in Tretha Yug, he would present himself in Dwapar Yug as Shree Madhav. In Kali Yug the Lord should be known by the name of Bindu Madhav.
Agni Bindu Rishi was extremely happy at the direct worship of Lord Vishnu and he prostrated before the Lord.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 60, Shlok 123
बिन्दुमाधवनामानं यो मामत्र समर्चयेत्
बिन्दुतीर्थकृतस्नानो निर्वाणं स हि विन्दति
(Lord Vishnu says), a devotee who takes bath in Bindu Teerth (presently Panch Ganga Ghat) and worships me as Bindu Madhav, attains Moksha.
Please watch our YouTube video on Bindu Madhav at the following Link :
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PnHNANHdVFM&t=17s
LOCATION OF BINDU MADHAV

Bindu Madhav is located at No. K.22/37, Panch Ganga Ghat. Devotees can approach this place by traveling upto Bhaironath in a rickshaw and walking on foot to this place. This is a famous temple. Alternatively, they can travel by boat upto Panch Ganga Ghat and climb the steps.

Panch Nada Teerth is now known as Panch Ganga Ghat and there is lot of divinity attached to this Ghat, especially during the month of Kartik. For details refer to Pancha Ganga Ghat mentioned elsewhere.
TYPES OF POOJA

The temple remains open from 04.00 a.m. to 08.00 p.m. Mangala Aarti is held at 04.00 a.m., Shringar Aarti at 08.00 a.m. and Shayan Aarti at 08.00 p.m. Kartik Month (Hindi) Shukla Ekadasi known as Prabodini Ekadasi is very important.
POOJARIES OF THE TEMPLE
Shri Murlidhar Ganesh Patwardhan is the poojary of the temple and he can be contacted in the Cell No. (0)9918936350 for performing any special pooja etc.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Adi Keshav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Primordial Form Who First Stepped into the Holy City (Varuna Sangam)
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> ADI KESHAV Kashi Khand, Chapter 69 mentions the various forms of Keshav (Lord Vishnu) in Varanasi. Lord Vishnu told Sage Bindu (details given under Bindu Madhav temple) that a devotee who worships him (Lord Vishnu) in the Lord’s form as Adi Keshav finds his sadness being cleansed away and will enjoy only happiness.
By worshipping Adi Keshav the devotee attains Mukti. Adi Keshav has installed Sangameshwar Ling at Varuna Ganga confluence and the former grants Moksha to the devotees.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 97, Shlok 15
वेदेश्वरादुदीच्यां तु क्षेत्रज्ञश्चादिकेशव:
दृष्टं त्रिभुवनं सर्वं तस्य संदर्षनाद्ध्रुवम्
By worshipping Aadi Keshav, located in the north of Vedeshwar, the devotee derives the benefits of worshipping the three worlds
(ADI KESHAV)

This entire area covering the temple is a Shakti Peet and any prayers will yield multiple benefits. Also, as this temple falls under the area of confluence of two rivers viz. Ganga and Varuna (Ganga Varuna Sangamam), the temple acquires religious power.
(GANGA VARUNA SANGAM) LOCATION OF ADI KESHAV Adi Keshav is located at A-37/51, Rajghat Fort. Devotees can travel upto this place by autorickshaw or cycle rickshaw or car.
Location of Adi Keshav temple as per google maps is given below :

https://www.google.com/maps/place/Adi+Keshav+Ghat/@25.3288669,83.0243932,15z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x398e2fc96ca9762f:0xd72c9629869ba96f!8m2!3d25.328868!4d83.0428259!16s%2Fg%2F11b6dy3165?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDEyOS4xIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D
Please watch our YouTube vide on Adi Keshav at the following Link :
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PnHNANHdVFM&t=17s TYPES OF POOJA The place of worship is open from 06.00 a.m. to 12.00 Noon and from 04.00 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. The timings may be flexible.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Narad Keshav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Form Associated with the Supreme Penance of Sage Narada
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> NARAD KESHAV Kashi Khand stated that Lord Vishnu is available in the form of Narad Keshav at Narad Teerth.
(NARAD KESHAV)

Devotees who take bath at Narad Teerth and worship Narad Keshav will be blessed by Lord Vishnu and they will gain ultimate knowledge in life. Narad Teerth is non existent now. It may be worth mentioning that in ancient times (may be 1000 – 2000 years back) there might have been various Teerths (Sacred ponds) etc. in Kashi. Now most of them have dried up. Wherever Kashi Khand mentions Teerth and if the Teerth is not available, devotees may take bath in River Ganga.
LOCATION OF NARAD KESHAV

Narad Keshav is located at A-10/80 Prahlad Ghat, inside Shitla Mandir opp. Prahladeshwar. People can approach this place by traveling in a rickshaw upto Prahlad Ghat Chauraha and then on foot. Alternatively they can take a boat ride upto Prahlad Ghat and climb the steps.
TYPES OF POOJA
The place of worship is open practically throughout and devotees can worship/perform any pooja by their own.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Prahlad Keshav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Guardian Form Dedicated to the Ultimate Child Devotee Prahlad
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> PRAHLAD KESHAV Lord Vishnu told Bindu Rishi, there is Prahlad Teerth where the Lord is existing in the form of Prahlad Keshav.
(PRAHLAD KESHAV)
Devotees who take bath in Prahlad Teerth and worship Prahlad Keshav will receive all sorts of blessings of Lord Vishnu. Prahlad Teerth is not existent now.
LOCATION OF PRAHLAD KESHAV

Prahlad Keshav is located at A-10/80 Prahlad Ghat inside Prahledeshwar temple, on the face of Ganges, on the right side wall. People can approach this place by traveling in a rickshaw upto Prahlad Ghat Chauraha and then on foot. Alternatively they can take a boat ride upto Prahlad Ghat and climb the steps.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple remains open from 06.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. and from 06.00 p.m. to 07.00 p.m. Aarti is held in the morning.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Yagya Varaha
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Sacrificial Boar Incarnation of Lord Vishnu (Panch Agni Akhada Ghat)
main_18_vishnu_temples.timings_text: Shri Shankaranand is the poojari of the temple. <div
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> YAGYA VARAHA Kashi Khand states one Yagya Varaha Teerth where Lord Vishnu is available in the form of Yagya Varaha.

Devotees who worship Yagya Varaha attain the benefits which will normally accrue when Yagya is performed. Here it is worth mentioning that performing any sort of Yagya is a great achievement and the benefits are manifold. Yagya Varaha Teerth is not in existence now.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 17
तीर्थे यज्ञवराहाख्ये यज्ञवाराहसंज्ञक:
नरै: समर्चनीयोऽहं सर्वयज्ञफलेप्सुभि:
(Vishnu Bhagwaan says), Then I am present in the form of Yagya Varaaha at Yagya Varaaha Teerth. Devotees desirous of getting fruits of performing various Yagyas, should worship me in that form.
LOCATION OF YAGYA VARAHA

Yagya Varaha is located at A.11/30, near Swarleeneshwar at Panch Agni Akhada Ghat. The temple is approachable from Prahalad Ghat Chauraha upto which place, people can travel by Auto or Cycle Rickshaw. Alternatively, they can have a boat ride upto Panch Agni Akhada Ghat and climb the steps.
TYPES OF POOJAS
The temple is open from 06.00 a.m to 9.00 p.m. Aarties are performed at 07.00 p.m.
POOJARIS OF THE TEMPLE
Shri Shankaranand is the poojari of the temple.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Vidar Narsimha
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: A Powerful, Defensive Half-Man, Half-Lion Manifestation
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> VIDAR NARSIMHA
Lord Vishnu blesses devotees in the form of Vidar Narsimha at the Teerth of the same name.
Devotees who worship Vidar Narsimha will see that all their obstacles are removed and they will be free from any sort of hindrance. The Teerth is not in existence now.
(VIDAR NARSIMHA)
LOCATION OF VIDAR NARSIMHA

Vidar Narsimha is located at A-10/82 Prahlad Ghat. People can approach this place by traveling in a rickshaw upto Birla Hospital after Macchodari and then on foot. Alternatively they can take a boat ride upto Prahlad Ghat and climb the steps.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple remains open from 04.30 a.m. to 12.00 Noon and from 04.00 p.m. to 09.00 p.m. Narsimha Jayanti is celebrated with great fervour on Vaishakh Shukla Triodashi.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Gopi Govind
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Cowherd Form Representing Protection and Pastoral Grace
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> GOPI GOVIND In Gopi Govind Teerth Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Gopi Govind.
Worshippers of Gopi Govind shall always be blessed by Lord Vishnu. The aforementioned Teerth is not in existence now.
LOCATION OF GOPI GOVIND

Gopi Govind is located at K.4/24, Lal Ghat near Birla Sanskrit Vidhyalaya, Birla House. Devotees can travel upto Bhaironath or Machhodari in a rickshaw and walk on foot to the place of Gopi Govind. Alternatively, they can travel by boat upto Lal Ghat and climb the steps. This temple also houses Narayani Devi (Lakshmi Devi) which has reference in Kashi Khand, Chapter 70.
TYPE OF POOJA
The temple is open from 07.00 a.m. to 10.00 p.m. Aarties are held in the morning.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Hayagreev Keshav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Horse-Headed Form Symbolizing Pure Knowledge and Wisdom
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> HAYAGREEVA KESHAV Kashi Khand mentions one Hayagreev Teerth where Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Hayagreev Keshav.
The devotees worshipping Hayagreev Keshav will reach Lord’s Lotus feet. Hayagreev Teerth is not in existence now.
(HAYAGREEV KESHAV)
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 23
हयग्रीवे महातीर्थे मां हयग्रीवकेशवम्
प्रणम्य प्राप्नुयान्नूनं तद्विष्णो: परमं पदम्
(Lord Vishnu Says) I am called present in form of Hargriva Keshava at Hayagriva Teerth. By simply worshipping me, a devotee surely attains the supreme post of Vishnu.
LOCATION OF HAYAGREEV KESHAV

Hayagreev Keshav is located at B.3/25 near Anandmayee Hospital at Bhadaini. People can reach this place by auto/car or cycle rickshaw. If one approaches from Sonarpura area, Hayagreev Keshav will be just before the Hospital. This place of worship also houses Hayagreeva Yogini which is mentioned in Kashi Khand, Chapter 45.
TYPES OF POOJA
The place is open for worship throughout.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Shwet Madhav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Radiant, Pure White Form Granting Supreme Spiritual Peace
main_18_vishnu_temples.timings_text: Shri Rajeshwar Prasad is the poojari of the temple.
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> SHWET MADHAV Kashi Khand mentions Lord Vishnu in the form of Shwet Madhav in the vicinity of Vishalakshi Devi.
Devotees who worship Shwet Madhav will attain the status equivalent to the Lord.
LOCATION OF SHWET MADHAV

Shwet Madhav is located at D.3/71, Big Hanuman temple at Mir Ghat. The deity is located in side the temple premises, exactly opposite Hanuman idol. Devotees can reach this place by traveling upto Dasaswamedh in a rickshaw and then on foot. Alternatively, they can take a boat ride upto Mir Ghat and climb the steps.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple is open from 07.00 a.m. to 01.00 p.m. and from 04.00 p.m. to 09.00 p.m. Aarties are held in the morning and evening.
POOJARIES OF THE TEMPLE
Shri Rajeshwar Prasad is the poojari of the temple.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Prayag Madhav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Form Connecting Kashi to the Sacred Confluence of Prayagraj (Dashashwamedh)
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> PRAYAG MADHAV Kashi Khand mentions Prayag Teerth where devotees have been advised to take bath and worship Prayag Madhav. Prayag Teerth has been mentioned to the north of Dasaswamedh.
A person worshipping Prayag Madhav will be cleansed of all his sins.
Kashi Khand has attached a great importance to bathing in Prayag Teerth. Prayag Teerth, as such, is not in existence but this falls within the larger area of Dasaswamedh.

One point needs to be mentioned here to make things clear. At the time when Skanda Puran was conceived by Bhagwan Ved Vyas and when the Puran was actually written, there were only five bathing places in Ganga at Varanasi, which had a great religious importance, namely Assi, Dasaswamedh, Manikarnika, Panchganga and Varuna. Even today, South Indian pilgrims who visit Varanasi, for their Kashi Yatra, perform Shraddha Karma at the above five Ghats. Over a period of several centuries, many Ghats have come up in the name of many Kings or the Royal families, etc. Religiously speaking, Dasaswamedh extends to a very wide area in the river Ganga and may include several new Ghats in its fold.

Therefore, Prayag Teerth as mentioned in Kashi Khand is a part of Dasaswamedh. Devotees may consider both as synonymous. Great importance has been attached to taking bath in the above Teerth in Magh Month and worshipping Prayag Madhav. Persons doing so, will be blessed with wealth, food grains, happy family and will attain Moksha.
LOCATION OF PRAYAG MADHAV

Prayag Madhav is located at D.17/111, in the premises of Ram Mandir at Dasaswamedh Ghat. Some people also call it Dharani Varaha (Ref: Varanasi Vaibhav by Pt. Kuber Nath Sukul). Devotees can travel upto Dasaswamedh Ghat in a rickshaw.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple remains opens for worship from 05.00 p.m. to 12.00 Noon and from 04.00 p.m. to 09.30 p.m. Timings may be flexible. Aarties are performed in the morning and evening.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Ganga Keshav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Manifestation Presiding Closely Over the Sacred Waters of the Ganges (Lalita Ghat)
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> GANGA KESHAV Kashi Khand mentions Ganga Keshav Teerth, where Lord Vishnu is present in the name of Ganga Keshav.
Intelligent devotees who worship Ganga Keshav will be respected and glorified in Vishnu Lok (Vaikunth).
(GANGA KESHAV)

Those who take bath in this Teerth and perform Shraddh Ceremony for their forefathers, with due donations etc. will satisfy their forefathers for over 100 years. While the Teerth is not in existence now, devotees may take bath in river Ganga. According to old timers, this Teerth may have merged with River Ganga.
LOCATION OF GANGA KESHAV

Ganga Keshav is located at D.1/67, Lalita Ghat, just above the steps. Devotees can travel upto Dasaswamedh Ghat in a rickshaw and it is easier to walk through Ghats rather than through Gullies to reach this place. Nepali Pasupatinath temple is a landmark below which, devotees can find Ganga Keshav, empanelled in eastern wall, opp. Shiv Ling.
Please watch our YouTube Video about Ganga Keshav at following Link
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xuyzf63HTdA&t=11s
TYPES OF POOJA
This place of worship is open practically through out and devotees can have darshan.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Vaikunth Madhav
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Earthly Baseline Representation of Vishnu's High Celestial Abode
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> VAIKUNTH MADHAV Towards the east of Vairochaneshwar, Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Vaikunth Madhav.
(VAIKUNTH MADHAV)

Devotees who worship this Lord with utmost devotion will derive the benefit of worshipping Lord Vishnu in Vaikunth. The implied meaning is that, after death, the devotee will reach Vaikunth (abode of Lord Vishnu).
LOCATION OF VAIKUNTH MADHAV

Vaikunth Madhav is located at Ck.7/165, near Harish-chandreshwar, Scindia Ghat. Devotees can reach this place by travelling upto Chowk in a rickshaw and then walking on foot via Sankata Devi temple which is a famous landmark.
TYPES OF POOJA
The deity is open for worship throughout. Devotees can perform pooja on their own.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Prachand Narsimha
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Exceedingly Fierce, Destructive Avatar Subduing Evildoers
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> PRACHAND NARSIMHA Kashi Khand states, towards the east of Chanda Bhairav, Lord Vishnu is present in the form Prachand Narsimha.
Prachand means huge/big. Devotees worshipping Prachand Narsimha are cleansed of all their sins irrespective of their magnitude.
(PRACHAND NARSIMHA)
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 190
प्रचण्ड नरसिम्होऽहं चण्डभैरवपूर्वत :
प्रचण्डमप्यघं कृत्वा निष्पाप्मा स्यात्तदर्चनात्
Lord Vishnu says, “Towards the east of Chand Bhairav, I am available as Prachand Narsimha and by worshipping this deity, the devotee will become sinless even after committing gravest of sins”.
LOCATION OF PRACHAND NARSIMHA
Prachand Narsimha is located at B.1/151, Jagannath Temple, Assi Ghat. People can travel upto this place in a rickshaw.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple is open from 06.00 a.m. to 12.00 noon and from 03.00 p.m. to 09.00 p.m. Aarties are held in the morning and evening.
Please watch our YouTube Video about Prachand Narsimha at following Link
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lb8jw8j5LEw&t=9s

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Atyugra Narsimha
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Terrifyingly Intense Half-Lion Form That Subdues Demonic Elements
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> ATYUGRA NARSIMHA Towards the north of Kamleshwar Siva, Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Atyugra Narsimha.
Devotees worshipping this Lord will be cleansed of all their sins. By splitting Atyugra readers can see the joining of two words Ati and Ugra. This shows the extreme power of this Lord.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 193
अत्युग्र नरसिंहोऽहं कलशेश्वरपश्चिमे
अत्युग्रमपि पापौघं हरामि श्रद्धयार्चित:
(Lord Vishnu says,) To the west of Kalasheshwar I am called Atyugra Narasimha. If I am worshipped with devotion, I destroy even the group of Atyugra (terrible) sins.
LOCATION OF ATYUGRA NARSIMHA
Atyugra Narsimha is located at Ck.8/21, Gomath. People can approach this place by traveling upto Chowk in a rickshaw and then on foot. Gomath is a famous locality.
TYPES OF POOJA
The place of worship is open from 06.00 a.m. to 10.00 a.m. and from 04.00 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. Devotees can pray and perform pooja by their own.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Kolahala Narasimha
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Loud, Roaring Narasimha Variant Representing Cosmic Primordial Sound
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> KOLAHALA NARSIMHA In the same locality of Atyugra Narsimha one can find Kolahala Narsimha.
(KOLAHAL NARASIMHA)
By worshipping this Lord, the sins will get topsy turvy and finally vanish.
LOCATION OF KOLAHALA NARSIMHA
Kolahala Narsimha is located at Ck.8/181 above Siddhi Vinayak, inside Narsimha Mutt. People can approach this place by traveling upto Chowk in a rickshaw and then on foot.
TYPES OF POOJA
The place of worship is open from 04.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. and from 05.00 p.m. to 09.30 p.m. Aarties are held in the morning and evening.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Vitank Narsimha
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Protective Shield Aspect Established Near Kedar Ghat
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> VITANK NARSIMHA Kashi Khand, in Chapter 61, mentions among other forms of Lord Vishnu, one Vitank Narsimha.
Devotees who worship this deity will always be courageous and gain mental strength which is vital for important decision making.
LOCATION OF VITANK NARSIMHA

Vitank Narsimha is located just outside the eastern door of Kedareshwar temple at B.6/102. This door faces the river Ganga. The idol of Vitank Narsimha is located at the steps of Kedar Ghat, on left side. Kedareshwar Temple, Kedar Ghat is a famous place and devotees can reach here by rickshaw, or by boat upto Kedar Ghat (river side).
TYPES OF POOJA
The place of worship is open throughout the day and devotees can worship as per their convenience.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Shri Kokavarah
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: A Rare, Early Puranic Variant of the Boar Avatar (Koka Teerth)
sanskrit_verses:
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 18
कोकवाराहसंज्ञोऽहं कोकातीर्थे व्यवस्थित: ।
तत्र स्नात्वा च मां दृष्ट्वा नरो दुर्गतिमश्नुते ॥

(Lord Vishnu states: "I am present in the form of Kokavarah at the holy Koka Teerth in Kashi. A devotee who bathes in this teerth and has my darshan will never fall into distress or hellish torment.")
main_18_vishnu_temples.location_text: Historically situated at Koka Teerth (in the sacred riverfront zone between Panchganga and Rajghat / Adi Keshav). In modern times worshipped alongside the Varaha sanctums at Panch Agni Akhada Ghat and Neelkanth.
main_18_vishnu_temples.timings_text: Open for darshan during standard ghat temple hours (06:00 AM to 08:30 PM).
paragraphs: Shri Kokavarah is an ancient and rare Puranic manifestation of Lord Vishnu in his boar (Varaha) avatar. In Chapter 61 of the Kashi Khand (Skanda Purana), Lord Vishnu recounts to Sage Bindu the principal forms in which he established his eternal presence across Varanasi.

Lord Vishnu declares that at Koka Teerth, he resides in the form of Kokavarah to dispel cosmic darkness, break the bonds of worldly entrapment (Samsara Bandhana), and preserve pilgrims from every kind of spiritual or physical distress.

According to traditional Kashi pilgrimage scriptures, bathing at the sacred riverfront associated with Koka Teerth and performing arghya and pranam to Kokavarah cleanses all ancestral debts and secures the divine protection of the preserver deity.
Pilgrims visiting the sacred Panchganga and Rajghat sectors pay homage to Kokavarah as the primordial defender against negative astral forces.

main_18_vishnu_temples.title: Shri Dharanivarah
main_18_vishnu_temples.designation: The Definitive Form of Varaha Lifting and Stabilizing the Earth (Dharani Teerth)
sanskrit_verses:
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 19
धरणीं समुद्धरन्पूर्वं वाराहेण वपुष्मता ।
धरणीधारको विष्णुरिह तिष्ठति सर्वदा ॥

("The supreme Lord Vishnu who lifted Mother Earth (Dharani) from the cosmic abyss upon his mighty tusk resides eternally in Kashi as Dharanivarah, sustaining all living beings.")
main_18_vishnu_temples.location_text: Located in the riverfront sector near Dharani Teerth / Panch Agni Akhada (adjoining Swarleeneshwar and Yagya Varaha at A.11/30). Easily accessible via Prahlad Ghat Chauraha or by boat to Panch Agni Akhada Ghat.
main_18_vishnu_temples.timings_text: Open from 06:00 AM to 09:00 PM. Evening aarti is performed around 07:00 PM.
paragraphs: Shri Dharanivarah is the definitive and celebrated cosmic form of Lord Vishnu who rescued and stabilized Mother Earth (Bhudevi / Dharani) during the cosmic cataclysm. When the demon Hiranyaksha dragged the earth into the primordial cosmic waters (Rasatala), Lord Vishnu assumed the gigantic, radiant form of the divine boar, vanquished the demon, and elevated the globe safely upon his tusk.

In Chapter 61 of the Kashi Khand, Lord Vishnu establishes that in Varanasi, he presides as Dharanivarah to bestow stability, firmness of character, agricultural abundance, and freedom from real-estate and planetary afflictions to his devotees.
Worshipping Dharanivarah at Varanasi connects the devotee to the foundational cosmic energy that stabilizes the earth itself, granting fearlessness and immense inner fortitude.
Devotees traditionally offer chandan (sandalwood paste), tulsi leaves, and yellow flowers to Dharanivarah while reciting the sacred Varaha Gayatri mantra.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Gyan Keshav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: Bestower of Pure Transcendental Wisdom and Intellect
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> GYAN KESHAV Kashi Khand mentions one Teerth known as Swet Deep and nearby is Gyan Keshav. Devotees who take bath in Swet Deep Teerth and worship Gyan Keshav will acquire ultimate knowledge.

While the Teerth is no longer visible, worshipping Gyan Keshav is considered good for education. Instead of taking bath in Teerth, now devotees take bath in river Ganges as this temple is exactly on the banks of river Ganges.
(GYAN KESHAV)
LOCATION OF GYAN KESHAV
Gyan Keshav is located at A-37/51, Adi Keshav Temple, Rajghat Fort. Devotees can travel upto this place by autorickshaw or cycle rickshaw or car.
Location of Adi Keshav Temple as per Google Maps is given below :

https://www.google.com/maps/place/Adi+Keshav+Ghat/@25.3288669,83.0243932,15z/data=!3m1!4b1!4m6!3m5!1s0x398e2fc96ca9762f:0xd72c9629869ba96f!8m2!3d25.328868!4d83.0428259!16s%2Fg%2F11b6dy3165?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI1MDEyOS4xIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D
TYPES OF POOJA The place of worship is open from 06.00 a.m. to 12.00 Noon and from 04.00 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. The timings may be flexible.
Please watch our YouTube Video about Gyan Keshav at following Link
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xuyzf63HTdA&t=11s

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Bhrigu Keshav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: Associated with the Austerities of Sage Bhrigu
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> BHRIGU KESHAV Lord Vishnu told Bindu Rishi, there is Bhargav Teerth where the Lord is existing in the form of Bhrigu Keshav.
Devotees who take bath in Bhargav Teerth and worship Bhrigu Keshav will receive all sorts of blessings of Lord Vishnu and their desires will be fulfilled. Bhargav Teerth is not existent now.
LOCATION OF BHRIGU KESHAV

Bhrigu Keshav is located at Gola Ghat on the steps aloft the river Ganga. People can approach this place by travelling in a rickshaw upto Prahlad Ghat crossroads and then on foot. Alternatively they can take a boat ride upto Gola Ghat and climb the steps.
TYPES OF POOJA
The place of worship is open practically throughout and devotees can worship/perform any pooja by their own.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Bheeshma Keshav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: Sanctum Established by Grandfather Bheeshma (Panchganga Ghat)
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> BHEESHMA KESHAV In the vicinity of Vriddha Kaleshwar one can find Bheeshma Keshav.
By worshipping Bheeshma Keshav even the most dangerous obstacles of the devotee will be removed.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 24
भीष्मकेशवनामाऽहं वृद्धकालेशपश्चिमे
उपसर्गान हरे भीषमान् सेवितो भक्तियुक्तित:
Lord Vishnu says, “By stationing myself as Bheeshma Keshav towards the west of Vriddh Kaaleshwar, I remove the dangerous disturbances of devotees who worship me with devotion.”
LOCATION OF BHEESHMA KESHAV
Bheeshma Keshav is located in the temple premises of Mrityunjay Mahadev at K.52/39, near Vriddha Kaleshwar. This place of worship is open throughout.
Please watch our YouTube video on Bheeshma Keshav at the following Link :
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PnHNANHdVFM&t=17s

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Vaman Keshav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Divine Dwarf Avatar Who Measured the Three Cosmic Worlds
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> VAMAN KESHAV Lord Vishnu mentions one Vaman Teerth where the Lord is existing in the name of Vaman Keshav.
Devotees who take bath in Vaman Teerth and worship Vaman Keshav will receive blessings of all round happiness. Vaman Teerth is not in existence now.
(VAMAN KESHAV)
LOCATION OF VAMAN KESHAV

Vaman Keshav is located at A.2/29, Trilochan. The temple is also known as Madhusudhan. The temple is approachable from Birla Hospital after Machhodari upto which place, people can travel by Auto or Cycle Rickshaw. Alternatively, they can have a boat ride upto Trilochan Ghat and climb the stairs. This deity is known by the name of Madhusudan. On Akshay Triteeya Day, many devotees worship this deity and they make offering of butter to the Lord.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple is open from 05.30 a.m. to 01.00 p.m. and from 03.00 p.m. to 09.00 p.m.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Tribhuwan Keshav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: Lord of the Three Worlds (Panchganga / Trilochan Zone)
sanskrit_verses: काश्यां ख्यातं त्रिभुवनकेशवं न स गर्भभाक्
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> TRIBHUWAN KESHAV In Tri Lok Sundari Vandi Devi’s South Kashi, Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Tribhuwan Keshav. (Kashi Khand mentions this as Bhuwan Keshav).
Devotees who worship Tribhuwan Keshav will not see womb again, meaning thereby that there will be no rebirth.
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 26
वन्ध्यास्त्रिलोकसुन्दर्या याम्यां यो मां समर्चयेत्
काश्यां ख्यातं त्रिभुवनकेशवं न स गर्भभाक्

(Lord Vishnu says) In Kashi to the south of Trilokya Sundari Bandi Devi, I am famous by the name Tribhuvan Keshav. The devotee who worships me here does not get rebirth. (That means he gets salvation).
LOCATION OF TRIBHUWAN KESHAV

Tribhuwan Keshav is located at D.17/100, Bandi Devi, Dasaswamedh Ghat. Just before the Ghat, devotees should take a right turn. It is advisable to enquire at the vegetable market just before the Ghat. The temple priest calls this deity by the name of Dharani Varaha. There is some confusion as some learned Pundits claim that Dharani Varaha is located at D.17/111, Ram Mandir and they give the name of Prayag Madhav for this.

Kashi Khand mentions South Kashi. If we take the Mukti Kshetra of Kashi as per Kashi Khand, Madhyameshwar is the mid point and Dasaswamedh Ghat falls to the South. However, in the present day scenario Dasaswamedh is the center point for various religious and cultural activities.
There is also a Shiv Ling in the temple premises which was called Prayageshwar by the Poojari.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple remains open from 08.00 a.m. to 11.00 a.m. However, devotees can have darshan through grilled door throughout.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Gyan Madhav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Dispeller of Spiritual Ignorance and Bestower of Enlightenment
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> GYAN MADHAV In front of Gyan Vapi Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Gyan Madhav.
By worshipping this Lord, the devotees will attain ultimate knowledge in all spheres of activities.
LOCATION OF GYAN MADHAV

Gyan Madhav is located at Ck.35/21, Vishwanath Temple compound near Akshay Vat. The narrow lane or Gully approaching the temple is known as Vishwanath Gully. For directions to reach this place, kindly refer Visweshwar Temple.
TYPES OF POOJA
Devotees can worship and pray this Lord as per their own convenience.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Veer Madhav
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Valorous and Heroic Aspect of Lord Vishnu in Kashi
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> VEER MADHAV Towards the north of Veereshwar, one can find Lord Vishnu in the form of Veer Madhav.
(VEER MADHAV)

A devotee who observes fast and performs Pooja of Veer Madhav will not face the wrath of Lord Yama. Kashi Khand is succinct in the narration. By the above paragraph, the readers can infer that the devotees who perform pooja of Veer Madhav will reach heaven.
LOCATION OF VEER MADHAV
There are two locations of Veer Madhav. One is near the door of Atma Veereshwar at Ck.7/158 (Rahu’s idol) and other is just opposite at Ck.7/30 where devotees can have darshan through window.
Devotees can reach this place by travelling upto Chowk in a rickshaw and then walking on foot via Sankata Devi temple which is a famous landmark.
TYPES OF POOJA
This place of worship is open throughout and devotees can perform pooja on their own.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Lakshmi Narsimha
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Gracious, Auspicious Form Accompanied by Goddess Lakshmi
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> LAKSHMI NARSIMHA Kashi Khand mentions one Lakshmi Narsimha Teerth where devotees should take bath and worship Lord Vishnu in the form of Lakshmi Narsimha.
(LAKSHMI NARSIMHA)
Such devotees would be blessed with all round happiness, prosperity and release from rebirth. The Teerth is not in existence as on date.
LOCATION OF LAKSHMI NARSIMHA

Lakshmi Narsimha is located at K.20/159, Raj Mandir, inside Dakshin Mukhi (one eyed) Hanumanji temple. This temple is near Kashi Vyayamshala / Suvodhini Vidya Mandir. Raj Mandir is a locality near Gai Ghat.
TYPES OF POOJA
The temple is open for worship from 06.00 a.m. to 12.00 Noon and from 02.00 p.m. to 10.00 p.m. Aarties are performed in the morning and evening.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Mahabal Narsimha
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Colossally Powerful Half-Lion Protector Deity
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> MAHABAL NARSIMHA Towards the eastern direction of Omkareshwar, Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Mahabal Narasimha.
Devotees worshipping Mahabal Narasimha will not see Yamdoot, meaning thereby they will reach heaven after death.
(MAHABAL NARSIMHA)
LOCATION OF MAHABAL NARSIMHA

Mahabal Narsimha is located at A-2/9 North of Trilochan, in the premises of Kameshwar Temple. The temple is approachable from a famous locality called Prahlad Ghat (after Machhodari). Devotees can travel beyond Machhodari upto Birla Hospital in a rickshaw and walk on foot to the temple.
TYPES OF POOJAS
The temple is open for worship from 05.00 a.m. to 12.00 Noon and 05.00 p.m. to 08.30 p.m. Mangala Aarti is held at 5.30 a.m. and Shayan Aarti at 09.30 p.m.
For doing special pooja, it is advisable to consult the Poojari before hand.
Please watch our YouTube Video about Mahabal Narsimha at following Link
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xuyzf63HTdA&t=11s
POOJARIS OF THE TEMPLE Shri Rajesh Giri is the Poojari of the temple and he can be contacted in his Cell number (0) 9839703054 for doing any special pooja etc.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Nar Narayan
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Primordial Twin Sages of Badrikashrama Manifested in Kashi
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> NAR NARAYAN
Kashi Khand states one Narayan Teerth where Lord Vishnu is available in the form of Nar Narayan.
Devotees who worship Nar Narayan will become equivalent to Lord Vishnu. Narayan Teerth is not in existence now.
LOCATION OF NAR NARAYAN

Nar Narayan (popularly known as Badri Narayan) is located at A.1/72, Badri Narayan Ghat steps near Gai Ghat. Devotees can approach this place by travelling upto Bhaironath in rickshaw and then on foot.
TYPE OF POOJA
The place is open for worship from 06.00 a.m. to 12.00 Noon. During other times, Darshan is allowed through open window. Name of the priest is Shri Dwarka Nath.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Trivikrama
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Three-Striding Lord of Boundless Cosmic Majesty
additional_vishnu_temples.timings_text: Pandit Girija Shankar Pandey is the Poojari of the temple and he can be contacted in his Cell number (0)9236511267 for doing any special pooja. <div
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> TRIVIKRAMA Towards the north of Trilochan, Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Trivikrama.
Devotees worshipping this Lord will be blessed with Lakshmi and their sins will be cleansed away. By Lakshmi, readers may infer wealth and prosperity.
(TRIVIKRAMA)
Kashi Khand, Chapter 61, Shlok 200
त्रिविक्रमोऽस्म्यहं काश्यामुदीच्यां च त्रिलोचनात्
ददामि पूजितो लक्ष्मीं हरामि वृजिनान्यपि
(Vishnu Bhagwan says) I am positioned in the form of Trivikram in north of Trilochan. I grant Lakshmi (prosperity) to devotees who worship me there and the sins of such devotees are destroyed by me.
LOCATION OF TRIVIKRAMA

Trivikrama is located at A-2/80, Trilochaneshwar Temple. Above the idol, it has been mentioned as Brihaspati. The temple is approachable from Birla Hospital after Machhodari upto which place, people can travel in Auto or Cycle Rickshaw. Alternatively, they can have a boat ride upto Trilochan Ghat and climb the stairs.
TYPES OF POOJAS

The temple is open for worship 05.30 a.m. to 12.00 noon and 05.00 p.m. to 11 p.m. Mangala Aarti is performed at 05.30 a.m. and Shayan Aarti at 11.00 p.m. For doing special pooja etc., it is advisable to consult the Poojari before hand.
POOJARIS OF THE TEMPLE
Pandit Girija Shankar Pandey is the Poojari of the temple and he can be contacted in his Cell number (0)9236511267 for doing any special pooja.

additional_vishnu_temples.title: Tamra Varaha
additional_vishnu_temples.designation: The Copper-Hued Boar Avatar Arrived from Tamra Dweep (Neelkanth Mohalla)
paragraphs: class="art-PostContent"> TAMRA VARAHA Lord Vishnu is present in the form of Tamra Varaha. This Varaha has come from Tamara Dweep.
(TAMRA VARAHA)
By worshipping Tamra Varaha, devotees will see their wishes and desires fulfilled.
LOCATION OF TAMRA VARAHA

Tamra Varaha is located outside House No.Ck.33/57, Neelkanth Mohalla in the slope. Devotees can travel upto Chowk in a rickshaw and walk on foot upto Neelkanth temple which is a famous landmark. Another landmark is Adi Chunchungiri Mutt of Karnataka.
TYPES OF POOJA
This place of worship is open throughout and devotees can perform pooja on their own.
Please watch our YouTube Video about Tamra Varaha at following Link https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lb8jw8j5LEw&t=9s
